title: Counit transpose of ordinary homotopy base change
statement: For a commutative square p f = f′ g of scheme morphisms and additive tensor pullbacks along all four arrows, let sigma be moduleHomotopyPullbackSquare [lem-pc-homotopy-pullback-square-localization]. For each homotopy complex D on X, sigma at f_*D followed by p* of the ordinary f tensor-adjunction counit equals the inverse f′ homotopy adjunction Hom equivalence of the termwise ordinary moduleBaseChangeMap [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-open-restriction], with homotopy composition identifications. No derived category or derived functor is used in this identity.

source.document: Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves and Derived Categories
source.place: Tag 08HY; the ordinary-mate identification step in lem-pc-derived-base-change-unit-compatibility.

proof.text: Define the ordinary pullback square as the composite of the inverse conjugates of the two sectionwise pushforward composition isomorphisms and the equality transport. Inverse conjugation reverses composition (Mathlib conjugateEquiv_symm_comp). For equality transport, substitute equal arrows and check pushforwardCongr on sections. Thus ordinarySquare_mate identifies this square with the inverse conjugate of the pushforward square. The inverse mate under the p and g tensor adjunctions is the natural transformation with components moduleBaseChangeMap: apply the g Hom equivalence, use its defining unit formula, and apply unit_mateEquiv_symm. Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm and mateEquiv_counit_symm then give ordinary_counit for every module.

Prove the generic map_counit identity for additive functors: represent any homotopy object as the quotient of a complex, expand the inverse Hom equivalence using homEquiv_counit, and use mapHomotopyCategory_counit_app_quotient. The mapped composition comparisons and mapped natural transformation are quotient images of the corresponding complex maps. Combine their composites by functoriality of the quotient. Equality of these complex maps follows degreewise from ordinary_counit; the composition comparisons for reflexivity have identity components. Apply this proved generic helper to ordinarySquare and the moduleBaseChangeMap natural transformation. The defining moduleHomotopyPullbackSquare is precisely this mapped square.

theorem moduleHomotopyBaseChange_counit
    {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (p : X' ⟶ X)
    (h : p ≫ f = f' ≫ g)
    [(Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f).Additive]
    [(Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f').Additive]
    [(Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).Additive]
    [(Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback p).Additive]
    (D : HomotopyCategory X.Modules (.up ℤ)) :
    let af := (Classical.choose
      (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction f)).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)
    let af' := (Classical.choose
      (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction f')).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)
    let b :=
      (Functor.mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso (Iso.refl
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f ⋙ Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).hom ≫
      NatTrans.mapHomotopyCategory
        { app := Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChangeMap f f' g p h
          naturality := fun _ _ a ↦
            Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChangeMap_naturality f f' g p h a }
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ≫
      (Functor.mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso (Iso.refl
        (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback p ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f'))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).inv
    (moduleHomotopyPullbackSquare f f' g p h).app
        (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj D) ≫
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback p).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).map
        (af.counit.app D) = (af'.homEquiv _ _).symm (b.app D)
